messages:
lina: quick heads-up — planning a tiny canary for tiltwave tomorrow 09:30 PT. rollout plan: 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% over ~90m. cohorts: us-west (sample bucket A) then eu-central (bucket B). deploy owner: @sam. smoke checks + rollback readiness below.

sam: ack, i'll own the deploy. @maya on metrics, @igor on rollback.

maya: good. what are the exact abort thresholds?

lina: abort if any of: p95 > 450ms sustained over 5m, 5xx rate >0.8% sustained 5m, or model error rate >1% on sampled requests. also abort on replication lag >30s.

igor: i'll be on standby with rollback playbook and kubectl access. ops-oncall, you good to monitor infra?

ops-oncall: noted — i'll watch infra dashboards and set a pager if redis or node CPU spikes. forwarding to incident channel.

deploy-bot: Scheduled deploy: tiltwave-canary at 2026-04-02T16:30:00Z (thread 5300001234). Rolling slices: 1% (T+10m), 5% (T+30m), 20% (T+90m). Approvers: sam, maya.

sam: preflight checklist: infra:green ✔️, migrations: none ✔️, feature-flag: canary-only set ✔️, secrets: validated ✔️. smoke script below.

sam: smoke test commands:
```
curl -sS https://tiltwave.canary/api/v1/health | jq .status
python tools/smoke_test.py --sample 50 --endpoint https://tiltwave.canary/generate --timeout 10
```

maya: i'll run the sample once 1% is up and post metrics. will also run a small rerank check.

lina: timeline recap: T0 deploy, +5m pods stabilize, +10m roll to 1% (smoke), +30m to 5% (smoke), +90m to 20% if all green. rollback window: immediate until 30m after final ramp.

igor: rollback commands ready:
```
kubectl rollout undo deployment/tiltwave --namespace=prod
# or pin prior revision:
kubectl set image deployment/tiltwave tiltwave=tiltwave:rev-20260301 --namespace=prod
```

maya: quick note — sample should exercise both text-gen and chat endpoints, set user-id header to sample buckets. I'll post exact curl commands when starting.

lina: add-ons: keep KV cache warmers on for canary, disable heavy background batch jobs during ramp window.

ops-oncall: will mute non-critical alerts for 40m to reduce noise; will keep latency/error pagers enabled.

sam: starting deploy in 5m. ping here when each ramp finishes.

deploy-bot: Deploy started — creating canary pods.

sam: deploy finished, canary pods are ready (3 pods).

maya: smoke run at 1%: 50 requests -> p95 210ms, avg 60ms, 5xx 0.0%. posting dashboard snapshot. :white_check_mark:

sam: progressing to 5%.

lina: reminder — watch redis tail latency and open file descriptors on the nodes.

ops-oncall: redis latency steady at 2ms, CPU 14%. nodes healthy.

maya: 5% smoke: 200 requests -> p95 230ms, avg 65ms, 5xx 0.2%. within thresholds.

sam: moving to 20% now.

maya: 20% smoke: initial sample (500 req) -> p95 440ms, avg 130ms, 5xx 0.9%. p95 is approaching abort threshold. monitoring 5m window.

lina: i'm seeing p95 tick up on the dashboard and a small uptick in model decode time. hold the ramp for 5m.

igor: standing by to rollback if p95 > 450ms for 5m or errors spike.

maya: after 3m running, p95 still ~445-460ms and error rate creeping to ~1.1% on retried requests. recommend abort and rollback.

sam: aborting ramp, initiating rollback now.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by sam.

sam: rollback in progress.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete — previous revision restored.

igor: confirmed: old revision running, pod counts back to baseline, health checks passing.

ops-oncall: infra metrics returning to baseline; redis stable.

maya: post-rollback quick metrics: p95 returned to ~220ms, errors 0.1%.

lina: postmortem action items (short): 1) Investigate KV cache hot-key pattern under 20% load, 2) tune model batch size or tokenizer bucket to reduce decode tail, 3) add a canary-only lighter decode config, 4) automate smoke run and abort on thresholds.

maya: created follow-up ticket INF-987 with traces and sample payloads.

sam: thanks team — good catch, nice coordination. :thumbsup:

security: noted. will review audit logs for canary requests and confirm no sensitive data exposure during tests.

lina: closing thread — we will reschedule a smaller config test next week and include shadow traffic tests before next ramp. Thanks everyone.
